- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 3-day bearish sentiment window.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+10% above 30d mean, reduce by 1–2% per 3-day lagged sentiment dip.
- For 30d horizon, model underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.0% to final 5–7 days of forecast if sentiment swings >0.33.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33/0.67 alternation), model overfits short-term momentum; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% per cycle.
